vendors.name: dbt Semantic Layer (MetricFlow)
vendors.tagline: Metric definitions in dbt projects. The open-source MetricFlow engine compiles them to SQL.
vendors.verdictNote: MetricFlow gives governed metrics. Agents query them through the dbt MCP server. The Semantic Layer APIs need a dbt Starter or higher plan.

artifacts.name: dbt Semantic Layer (semantic models and metrics in YAML)
dbt MCP server OAuth for AI tools (labeled Beta)
Apache Ossie semantic layer documents (dbt v1.12 and later)

metrics.n: Users define metrics in YAML (simple, ratio, derived, cumulative, conversion). MetricFlow compiles them to SQL for each warehouse.

dimensions.n: Users declare categorical and time dimensions on model columns, with time granularity. MetricFlow adds joins at query time.

relationships.n: Entities (primary, foreign, unique, natural) mark join keys. MetricFlow builds joins across semantic models from them.

synonyms.n: Semantic models, dimensions, and metrics have description and label fields. The docs show no synonyms field.

verifiedQueries.n: No question-to-SQL store exists. Saved queries (GA) group metrics, dimensions, and filters. The MCP list_saved_queries tool returns them.

nl2sql.n: The MCP text_to_sql tool generates SQL from project context. It uses dbt Copilot actions. It is off when AI is disabled.

ontology.n: No separate ontology layer exists. Teams model entities, dimensions, and metrics in semantic models.

graph.n: No graph query language exists. Semantic models form a join graph that MetricFlow uses internally.

vector.n: The MCP get_related_models tool finds similar models with semantic search. The broader search tool is labeled Alpha.

mcp.n: The MCP server has Semantic Layer, Discovery, SQL, and Admin API tools. The remote server is on all plans. Tools vary by plan.

governance.n: Queries run under a warehouse credential, so platform access policies apply. The Discovery API and MCP expose lineage. Plan limits apply.

openStandard.n: MetricFlow is Apache 2.0. dbt v1.12 and later also read Apache Ossie JSON documents as semantic models.

offers: Users define metrics, entities, and dimensions once in YAML. MetricFlow compiles them to SQL, so agents do not write joins.
The MCP server tools list metrics, get dimensions, query metrics, and run text_to_sql.
Saved queries group common metric and dimension combinations. MCP lists them.
MetricFlow is Apache 2.0. dbt v1.12 reads Apache Ossie documents.
It works with Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, Postgres, and Trino.
gaps: It answers only modeled questions. In the dbt April 2026 benchmark, questions that needed too many entity hops got no answer.
The Semantic Layer APIs and integrations need a dbt Starter, Enterprise, or Enterprise+ plan.
No synonyms field exists. Only description and label carry business wording.
The product has no stored question-to-SQL pairs and no ontology layer.
fillWith: Text-to-SQL for questions outside the model
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model your core metrics and dimensions in dbt. Then connect an agent through the dbt MCP server. Let the agent query metrics for modeled questions. Use text-to-SQL only for questions outside the model.

snippet.title: Semantic model on a dbt model (dbt v1.12 and later)
snippet.code:
models:
  - name: fact_transactions
    semantic_model:
      enabled: true
    agg_time_dimension: transaction_date
    columns:
      - name: transaction_date
        granularity: day
        dimension:
          type: time
    metrics:
      - name: transaction_total
        type: simple
        agg: sum
        expr: transaction_total

vendors.name: Cube (Core and Cloud)
vendors.tagline: Semantic layer with cubes and views, plus Cloud agents, Analytics Chat, and MCP.
vendors.verdictNote: The docs describe cubes, views, access policies, AI context, certified queries, a Chat API, a hosted MCP server, and Ossie conversion (Preview).

artifacts.name: Chat API for Cube agents (Premium and Enterprise plans)
AI context and certified queries (code-first agent config)

metrics.n: Users declare measures in cubes (count, sum, filtered measures). Views expose them to consumers.

dimensions.n: Users declare dimensions, hierarchies, and time dimensions in cubes. Views include them.

relationships.n: Joins between cubes declare a relationship (such as many_to_one). Views use join_path to pick the route.

synonyms.n: The agent reads descriptions. The ai_context field in meta on views and members is agent-only. It has up to 2,000 characters.

verifiedQueries.n: Certified queries are Markdown files with a user_request and SQL. The agent uses them as trusted examples.

nl2sql.n: Analytics Chat and the Chat API answer questions over the semantic layer. The Chat API needs a Premium or Enterprise plan.

ontology.n: The docs show no ontology layer. Cubes and views are the modeling objects.

graph.n: The docs show no graph query language.

vector.n: The docs index shows no vector or semantic search feature.

mcp.n: The hosted MCP server uses OAuth and is available on all plans. The earlier local npm server is deprecated.

governance.n: Access policies combine member access, row filters, and masking by group. Analytics Chat honors the active security context.

openStandard.n: Apache Ossie export and import work through the Cube CLI and Platform API. The docs label it Preview. Contact support to enable it.

offers: Cubes and views give agents a curated, joined model. Users define measures and dimensions once.
The hosted MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor query governed data over OAuth.
Agent configuration lives in the repo. It has rules, certified queries, and accessible views.
Descriptions and the agent-only ai_context in meta guide the agent.
Access policies with row filters and masking apply to agent queries.
gaps: Cube reads only SQL-queryable sources. It does not read files or REST APIs directly.
The Chat API needs a Premium or Enterprise plan.
Cube deprecated agent configuration in the UI. Code-first setup replaces it.
Ossie conversion and Evals are Preview. Cube support activates Ossie conversion.
The docs show no ontology, graph, or vector feature.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model cubes and views on your warehouse. Then expose a small set of views to an agent. Use the hosted MCP server or the Chat API. Add rules, ai_context, and certified queries under the agents directory.

snippet.title: A cube with a join, a measure, and a dimension
snippet.code:
cubes:
  - name: users
    sql_table: users

    joins:
      - name: organizations
        relationship: many_to_one
        sql: "{CUBE.organization_id} = {organizations.id}"

    measures:
      - name: count
        type: count
        sql: id

    dimensions:
      - name: country
        sql: country
        type: string

vendors.name: AtScale
vendors.tagline: Enterprise semantic layer with an open modeling language (SML) and an MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: AtScale models governed metrics in SML, an open YAML format. It serves them to agents through an MCP server.

artifacts.name: Semantic models in Semantic Modeling Language (SML), Apache open source
Natural Language Query (NLQ), announced as private preview
AtScale for Snowflake Semantic Views (XMLA endpoint, private preview coming soon)

metrics.n: Metric and calculation objects in SML define aggregated and derived values. These include semi-additive and non-additive metrics.

dimensions.n: Dimension objects declare attributes and hierarchies for drill-down. SML also covers time-based levels.

relationships.n: Model files declare relationships between fact datasets and dimensions. These include role-playing relationships.

synonyms.n: Models, dimensions, and metrics have description and label fields. MCP column tools return descriptions. The docs show no synonyms field.

verifiedQueries.n: The SML reference and MCP tools show no stored question-to-SQL examples. The MCP get_sml_skills tool serves query guidance.

nl2sql.n: External agents write SQL through MCP run_query. AtScale announced a first-party NLQ feature as private preview in Sept 2024.

ontology.n: The SML object list shows no ontology layer. Objects are models, dimensions, metrics, calculations, and datasets.

graph.n: The SML reference and MCP tools show no graph query language.

vector.n: The MCP tools and SML reference show no vector search.

mcp.n: MCP server tools: list_models, explore_columns, focus_columns, run_query, get_outbound_queries. Helm values enable them.

governance.n: Row security objects restrict rows by user or group. The MCP outbound query audit needs the queries_view role.

openStandard.n: SML is Apache open source with converters and a CLI. AtScale joined the Open Semantic Interchange on 27 Jan 2026.

offers: SML models metrics, dimensions with hierarchies, and relationships. SML is a YAML format that teams keep in Git.
MCP run_query checks agent SQL against the model before it reaches the warehouse.
MCP column tools return descriptions and sampled values for each column.
Row security objects restrict data by user or group.
The MCP server is in the Databricks MCP Marketplace. The listing dates from Dec 2025.
gaps: The docs show no stored question-to-SQL examples and no synonyms field.
AtScale announced first-party NLQ as a private preview in Sept 2024. The current docs describe MCP access for external agents.
MCP queries must be SELECT only. They must use one model per query. They must not use CTEs or subqueries.
The current docs list six warehouses. AtScale announced the Snowflake Semantic Views endpoint but did not ship it.
Only SML is open source. The engine is a commercial product.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model metrics in AtScale. Enable the MCP server in your Helm values. Point your agent at list_models, explore_columns, and run_query. The agent then uses governed metrics instead of raw tables.

snippet.title: An SML metric object
snippet.code:
unique_name: m_catalog_sales_coupon_amount_avg
object_type: metric
label: Catalog Sales Average Coupon Amount
calculation_method: average
dataset: catalog_sales
column: cs_sales_price

vendors.name: Wren AI / Wren Engine
vendors.tagline: Open-core GenBI engine and context layer with a modeling definition language (MDL).
vendors.verdictNote: Wren is an open-source semantic engine. It has MDL models, relationships, cubes, NL-to-SQL pairs, an MCP server, and Apache Ossie import and export.

artifacts.name: Modeling Definition Language (MDL) project: models, relationships, views, cubes
Knowledge base: rules and NL-to-SQL pairs with memory index

metrics.n: Cubes declare measures as expression plus type on a base model or view. Users query them with wren cube query.

dimensions.n: Cubes declare dimensions, time dimensions with query-time granularity, and hierarchies. Models declare typed columns.

relationships.n: The relationships.yml file declares a join type (such as MANY_TO_ONE) and an equality condition between two models.

synonyms.n: Models and columns have properties.description. Agents also retrieve Markdown rules and glossary files under knowledge/.

verifiedQueries.n: NL-to-SQL pairs are Markdown files under knowledge/sql/. The wren memory store command writes them.

nl2sql.n: Agents generate governed SQL through wren query and wren ask. Wren AI Cloud adds a GenBI UI.

ontology.n: The MDL reference shows no ontology layer. Models, relationships, views, and cubes are the objects.

graph.n: The MDL reference and CLI show no graph query language.

vector.n: A local LanceDB memory index gives hybrid retrieval over schema and stored pairs. It needs the memory extra.

mcp.n: The wren serve mcp command exposes query, dry-run, schema, and knowledge tools over stdio or HTTP. It needs the mcp extra.

governance.n: Row and column security is in Wren AI Cloud and Enterprise Plus. It is not in open source. OSS can omit model columns.

openStandard.n: The engine, SDK, and skills are Apache 2.0. Wren reads and writes Apache Ossie 0.1.1 and the 0.2.0.dev0 draft.

offers: MDL models, relationships, views, and cubes live as YAML in Git.
Agents recall NL-to-SQL pairs and business rules that are stored under knowledge/.
A local MCP server has query, dry-run, schema, and knowledge tools.
Wren imports from dbt, OpenMetadata, and Apache Ossie. It exports to Ossie.
Wren connects to the data sources in the connect guide on one Apache DataFusion engine.
gaps: Row and column security, the GenBI UI, and dashboards are commercial (Wren AI Cloud or Enterprise Plus).
Wren does not support traversal of a relationship handle directly in a query yet (issue 2688).
The docs list the golden NL-SQL eval runner as in development.
The connect guide lists fewer data sources than the README figure of 22+.
No ontology or graph feature exists.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Install the CLI with pip install wrenai. Generate or import an MDL project. Add rules and NL-to-SQL pairs under knowledge/. Connect your agent through wren serve mcp or the Wren skills. Query with wren query.

snippet.title: MDL model on a physical table
snippet.code:
name: customers
table_reference:
  catalog: jaffle_shop
  schema: main
  table: customers
primary_key: customer_id
columns:
  - name: customer_id
    type: INTEGER
    is_primary_key: true
    not_null: true
  - name: first_name
    type: VARCHAR

vendors.name: Malloy (with Publisher)
vendors.tagline: Open-source semantic modeling and query language. Publisher serves models with an MCP endpoint.
vendors.verdictNote: Malloy models define sources, joins, and measures in code. Publisher serves them to agents through an MCP endpoint.

artifacts.name: Malloy semantic models (sources, joins, dimensions, measures, views)
Malloy Publisher (server, REST API, web UI)

metrics.n: Measures use aggregate expressions on sources. The model stores them.

dimensions.n: Users declare dimensions and views on sources. Views are saved queries that agents can reuse.

relationships.n: The join_one, join_many, and join_cross keywords declare joins on a source. Primary keys enable the with shortcut.

synonyms.n: Annotations on fields and sources carry descriptions. Agents read them through Publisher. The docs show no synonyms field.

verifiedQueries.n: No question-to-query store exists. malloy_getContext returns named views and queries to guide agents.

nl2sql.n: Malloy has no first-party NL-to-query generation. malloy_getContext retrieves relevant fields for a question. The agent writes the Malloy.

ontology.n: The language reference and Publisher docs show no ontology layer.

graph.n: No graph query language exists. Malloy models joins as a data graph for correct aggregation. Queries are not graph queries.

vector.n: The Malloy and Publisher docs show no vector search.

mcp.n: Publisher serves MCP at localhost:4040/mcp. It has discovery, query, compile, reload, and docs search tools.

governance.n: Givens, #(authorize), and #(access_filter) gate sources and rows. Givens are behind an experimental flag. Publisher has no built-in authentication.

openStandard.n: Malloy is MIT-licensed open source. The docs show no Apache Ossie import or export.

offers: Users write models in code with sources, joins, dimensions, and measures. Malloy compiles them to each database dialect.
Publisher serves models over REST, a web UI, and MCP.
malloy_getContext finds relevant sources, views, and fields for a plain-English question.
malloy_compile checks agent-written Malloy. It returns diagnostics and does not run a query.
Malloy supports DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, Postgres, MySQL, Trino, and Presto.
gaps: No first-party NL-to-SQL, verified-query store, or synonyms field exists. The agent writes Malloy.
Publisher has no built-in authentication, and its MCP port is open. Put a gateway in front of it.
Row-level access relies on givens. Givens are behind an experimental flag.
The docs show no Apache Ossie import or export.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Write Malloy models for your core sources. Run Publisher. Point your agent at its MCP endpoint. Add annotations and named views so the agent finds the right fields. Test that your LLM writes valid Malloy.

snippet.title: Malloy sources with a primary key, a measure, and a join

vendors.name: Honeydew
vendors.tagline: Semantic layer defined in YAML, with an AI analyst, APIs, and an MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: Entities, attributes, metrics, and relations are first-party objects. The product also has Deep Analysis, an MCP server, row-level security, and Apache Ossie import and export.

artifacts.name: Context layer (instructions, skills, external knowledge, memory)
Snowflake Native App (semantic query and model update API)
Apache Ossie converter (import and export, tracks draft spec)

metrics.n: Metrics are aggregations. Users define them once at an entity granularity. The engine recomputes them for any slice or join.

dimensions.n: Entities have source and calculated attributes. Domains choose which fields the model exposes.

relationships.n: Entities declare relations with rel_type and key fields. Honeydew finds the join path from them.

synonyms.n: AI metadata on domains, entities, attributes, and metrics holds descriptions, synonyms, and allowed values.

verifiedQueries.n: The docs show no verified question-to-SQL store. Agents take sample questions for routing. Context items hold instructions and skills.

nl2sql.n: Deep Analysis runs multi-step analysis. The semantic compiler writes the SQL, not the LLM. Users also reach it from Slack, Teams, and MCP.

ontology.n: No ontology layer exists. Entities, relations, and domains are the modeling objects.

graph.n: No graph query language exists. The GraphQL API exposes the platform, not graph queries.

vector.n: The docs show no vector search.

mcp.n: The MCP server at mcp.honeydew.cloud uses OAuth. Tools cover analysis, model browsing, warehouse discovery, and model editing.

governance.n: Security includes row-level security via domain filters or warehouse policies, user access control, Git change approval, and CI/CD.

openStandard.n: A bidirectional Apache Ossie converter lives in the Ossie repository. It tracks a draft spec that may change.

offers: Users define metrics once per entity. The engine resolves join paths from declared relations.
AI metadata holds descriptions, synonyms, and allowed values on entities, attributes, and metrics.
Deep Analysis and agents answer questions. The semantic compiler compiles the SQL.
The MCP server works with Claude, Cursor, Snowflake Intelligence, and other clients.
Honeydew has row-level security, user access control, and Git workflows for model changes.
Honeydew imports and exports with Apache Ossie.
gaps: Snowflake is the GA platform. Databricks and BigQuery support are Beta. Support must enable them.
No stored question-to-SQL pairs exist. Sample questions only route questions to agents.
The Apache Ossie spec is an early draft, so the converter may change.
The docs show no ontology, graph, or vector feature.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Define entities, relations, and metrics in a Honeydew workspace. Expose a domain to an agent. Add AI metadata with synonyms. Use Deep Analysis, or connect your own agent or Snowflake Cortex Agents through the MCP server.

snippet.title: A metric defined on an entity
snippet.code:
type: metric
entity: lineitem
name: revenue
description: revenue, as defined in TPC-H Q3, Q5 and others
datatype: number
sql: |-
  sum(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount))

notes.text: Vendor-run by dbt Labs. The blog is dated 7 Apr 2026. The dataset is ACME Insurance (from data.world), with 11 questions run 20 times each. On the original schema (all 11 questions), text-to-SQL scored 64.5% and the Semantic Layer scored 72.7%. Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.3 Codex both gave these scores. After dbt added 3 models, the Semantic Layer scored 98.2% (Sonnet 4.6) and 100.0% (GPT-5.3 Codex). Text-to-SQL scored 90.0% and 84.1%. Bodo (Sep 2026) reported 220 of 220 correct with its own PyDough pipeline on a local SQLite replica. That setup is not the dbt setup.

sources.t: Semantic Layer vs. Text-to-SQL: 2026 Benchmark Update (dbt)
dbt Discourse thread on the benchmark

notes.text: Vendor-run by Cube staff. The blog and arXiv paper are dated 28 Apr 2026. The dataset is Cleaned Contoso Retail in ClickHouse, with 100 questions, single-shot. A 4 KB hand-written markdown semantic document added to the schema raised accuracy. Opus 4.7 rose from 50.5% to 67.7%. Sonnet 4.6 rose from 46.5% to 68.7%. GPT-5.4 rose from 45.5% to 68.7%. The semantic layer in this test was the markdown file. It was not a running Cube deployment.

sources.t: Cube blog: paired benchmark across three frontier models

notes.text: Vendor-run by AtScale. The white paper blog is dated 8 Aug 2024. The dataset is TPC-DS, with 40 questions and 3 retries allowed on SQL syntax errors. A control that had only table schemas and primary and foreign keys scored 20%. The AtScale semantic layer with its query engine scored 92.5%. The blog does not name the LLM. AtScale launched a public text-to-SQL leaderboard on 6 Nov 2024.

sources.t: AtScale: natural language prompting with semantic layer and GenAI

notes.topic: Apache Ossie status for these vendors
notes.text: OSI has a new name: Apache Ossie (incubating). dbt v1.12 reads Ossie JSON documents. Wren and Honeydew document import and export. Cube documents conversion as Preview (changelog 16 Oct 2026). AtScale joined OSI on 27 Jan 2026. The Malloy docs show no Ossie support.

sources.t: dbt: Apache Ossie semantic layer documents

notes.text: Cube hosts a remote MCP server at cubecloud.dev/mcp with OAuth. The README says the remote server replaces the earlier local npm package, which is deprecated.
Honeydew docs mark Snowflake as the supported platform. They label Databricks and Google BigQuery support as Beta, available through support.
Current Wren docs define MDL as YAML files that compile to target/mdl.json. Older material shows MDL as JSON.
